sermon.title: Magnifical House Reviewed
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In “Magnifical House Reviewed,” Pastor David G. Kincer revisits 1 Chronicles 22:5’s exceeding magnifical house and applies it to the church as living stones (1 Peter 2:5)—strong like a three-fold cord when united with word and Jesus. He says imperfect people (strangers who built with Solomon, Peter, Paul, Thomas) can still serve, that God’s presence must meet and speak, and that four things belong in the house: prayer, praise/presence, and the living word that makes disciples. He closes from Isaiah 2 that swords-to-plowshares has not yet been fulfilled and needs a magnifical church.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Caption “1st chronicles 20 25” read as 1 Chronicles 22:5 (the “exceeding magnifical” verse; flag for Michael). magnifico/magnificum→magnifical; mist→midst; asaph/haman/judgeth→Asaph/Heman/Jeduthun; drunk→drum; cheapest center→chiefest sinner; tongue brothel→tongue bridled; Luke 16 not 69→Luke 6:19; win→wind; calm→come; ha silver/so moneo→[unclear] law types. He calls Solomon’s foreign laborers “illegal aliens”—kept as spoken. Critique of psychology/psychiatry, prosperity, music-group idolatry, and “rapture as magical answer” kept as spoken.

chunks.section_question: What is the three-fold cord for the church?
chunks.short_answer: Believers are weak fibers alone; united with other members, the word and Jesus they become a cord the gates of hell cannot prevail against—strong, great and large throughout the earth.
chunks.text: strong, like a three-fold cord. A three-fold cord is made of fibers—that’s us, we’re the little fibers. Alone we’re weak, but when we unite with other church members and other fibers and we get into unity we make the church and we become strong. And when we unite with the word of God and with Jesus—a three-fold cord—we become a group that the gates of hell cannot prevail against. And so God wants the church to be strong, He wants it to be great, and He wants it to be large, and it is—it spread throughout all the earth today.

chunks.section_question: Were Peter, Paul and Thomas still used after failure?
chunks.short_answer: Peter denied, others fled and fished; Paul was chief sinner yet built the church; critical Thomas still was used. God chooses the foolish and weak to shame the wise (1 Corinthians 1:26).
chunks.text:
That restrains folks. In the New Testament, Peter cursed and denied God and still was used of God. The rest ran when Jesus was crucified and still were used of God. All went fishing. Paul didn’t marry; he killed innocent blood; he blasphemed the Holy Ghost and persecuted the church. The Bible says he was the world’s chiefest sinner—number uno sinner, number one—and God saved him and he became a part to build the church. Thomas was a discourager. Jesus said I’m going to go and raise Lazarus from the dead, and they said what’s the matter with you, don’t you know they tried to kill you when we were there last time? And He says, well, I’m going. And Thomas turns to the rest of the apostles and says, well, let’s go and die with him.

We have so many people that criticize the church and speak discouragingly that it’s a wonder we can get anything done. But I want to tell you something: Thomas was used of God in spite of his discouraging critical talk. 1 Corinthians 1:26: you see your calling, brethren, your invitation. God chose the foolish, the weak, the inferior, the despised things of this world and the things that are not. I’m not mature yet. I haven’t got my tongue bridled yet. I’m not in control of myself yet. He chose these kind of people to shame the wise and the intellectual of this world—New Testament church.

chunks.section_question: Why is God’s presence top priority in services?
chunks.short_answer: Acts 4 shaking, Paul’s Damascus encounter, and John 16:8 conviction show His presence convinces of sin, righteousness and judgment—and Luke 6:19 virtue healed all who touched Jesus.
chunks.text:
Himself but through people. In Acts 4 the place was shaken where they were gathered together to pray and they spoke the word of God with boldness. Paul on the road to Damascus saw a light and heard a voice. He had an encounter with God. It blinded him. Then his blinded eyes were opened and he became the chief apostle to build this magnifical church that God had prophesied thousands of years before that He would do. The encounter also convicts us. John 16:8: when the Holy Spirit, the Comforter, has come, He will convict the world of sin, righteousness and judgment. That presence of God, when it touches you, will convince you of right and wrong and that there’s a judgment coming.

We need the presence of God in our services—top priority, top priority. Then we find also in the Bible that the virtue, the power of God—that power of His presence—did tremendous things. In Luke 6:19 the whole multitude sought to touch Jesus, and there went virtue out of Him and healed them all—physically, mentally, spiritually, their sin. Power went out and healed them. Folks, that’s what people need to touch when they come to church: the power of His presence. That’s what does the job.

And He said to them, “It is written, ‘My house shall be called a house of prayer,’ but you have made it a ‘den of thieves.’ ”
and that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in His name to all nations, beginning at Jerusalem.

chunks.section_question: What does he say destroyed past awakenings in America?
chunks.short_answer: About 30 years after the last awakening, he says music-group idolatry, making gods of faith and prosperity, and psychology/psychiatry replaced what only Spirit and word can do—crowds without change into His image.
chunks.text:
By a 12-step program? No—by the Spirit of the Lord. Folks, that’s why we need Him. That’s why worship and praise is so necessary. These people that say what kind of God’s up there wanting everybody to praise Him and thank Him—it’s a principle that releases the power. He’s not up there with an ego. It’s a principle that works. And so when we do our part He will come by His Holy Spirit and do His part. But if we’re not looking for the Holy Ghost and we’re not looking for the presence of God, we’re just going to have a social gathering. There’s not going to be any power. We’ll have a meeting with music, we’ll have a meeting with people, we’ll fellowship with our friends, we’re going to go home unchanged, because it’s the Spirit that changes us into His image, and it’s His image that we’re after—not the popular author of the day. Matthew 21:13: My house shall be called the house of prayer, but you made it a den of thieves. We are in a 30th year after the last spiritual awakening in America, and we destroyed that awakening—the Jesus movement and the charismatic movement before that and the healing movement before that. We destroyed that by turning to music groups, making a god out of faith, making a god out of prosperity, and then bringing in psychology and psychiatry into the church to

do what only the Spirit and the word can do. And we brought this on ourselves. But we’re trusting God will move again. How many people will come to church if all you do is pray for an hour? But you get a music group or a mime or a drama or something and they’ll come—“oh we got a thousand people out there”—but did they get changed when they were there into His image? That’s the bottom line. Psalm 100 says serve the Lord with gladness and come before His presence. After prayer we need His presence. We don’t need the presence of the song leader and a preacher and the ushers and so forth. The main ingredient in a church service, a New Testament, is He’s there. And He tells us how to come into His presence with praise and worship and singing and clapping and so forth. Psalm 100 verse 4: enter His gates—number three—with thanksgiving, His courts with praise; be thankful unto Him and bless His name. Speak good of His name, exalt His name, exalt Jesus, thank Jesus, glorify Jesus, build up Jesus, brag about Jesus. That’s how we’re supposed to come to the house of God—not “oh I wonder who the server is going to pick me up today.” I wonder—how we’re supposed to come: on fire, prepared.

And when we do, His presence will come, because Psalm 22:3 says He inhabits the praises of His people. It’s a principle of praise. It’s not an egotistical God that the atheists try to say—what kind of God wants to be—but it is a principle He’s ordained that works, and when we operate it He will back it up. Luke 24:47: repentance and remission of sins should be preached in His name among the nations. So the fourth thing is we’ve got to have the word of God—the rhema word of God, the living word of God—and repentance and forgiveness and cleansing and freedom of sin should be preached. And it’s not being preached very much in America today because the church in America don’t want to hear they’re wrong. But they’re wrong whether they like to hear it or not. And we’ve got to get back to letting people know what sin is and they can repent from it and they can be forgiven, set free and cleansed from it. And that makes a magnifical church.

And it should be done to all nations. No one is eliminated from this. They need to hear that message. Still on number four, the second part: Matthew 28:19, go and make disciples of all nations, teaching them to observe all things that I have commanded you—what He’s commanded, not what psychologists commanded, what theologians command. It’s what He commands, what He told us to teach. And every expression of speech—whether it’s songs, prophecy, revelation, tongues, interpretation, wisdom, knowledge, teaching, prayer—is to build and change the people that are in that service unto His image. Our songs have got to be songs that build, construct and strengthen people. Our messages, our prophecies, everything is to build and make people a strong magnifical person for Jesus Christ so we can be changed into His image. Now Isaiah prophesied this years before, hundreds of years before. Isaiah 2:3: many shall go and say, come, let us go up to the house of the God of Jacob.

chunks.section_question: Has Isaiah 2’s peace among nations been fulfilled?
chunks.short_answer: He says no—swords into plowshares has not happened—and rejects treating the rapture as a magical answer. When the church becomes magnifical with His presence teaching His paths, Jesus can bring it to pass; without Him the American church tries in vain.
chunks.text:
He will teach us His ways and we will walk in His paths. There’s that word again: He will teach us. The Holy Ghost would teach us. The presence of Jesus would teach us. And we will walk in His paths. Why? Because the Holy Ghost would convict us. The Holy Ghost will empower us to obey the word, not just hear it. For out of Zion—and Hebrews 12 tells us Zion is the church, and Zion is the new city of Jerusalem, the church—out of the church will go forth the law—[unclear] law, [unclear] law, and spiritual law—and the word of the Lord, what He commanded us to teach, from Jerusalem, from the church. So the word is supposed to go from the church, is supposed to be in the church—a living word, a powerful word from the Holy Spirit. And then look at the results when we do these things: He will judge among the nations, He will correct many people, they will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war anymore. And I submit to you: has this ever been fulfilled? No. Well, why do you think the rapture is some kind of magical answer when this is just one of the things in the Bible that has not been fulfilled? But when we get our act together and become

a magnifical church that He’s building in these last days, He will have no problem bringing this to pass. He is Jesus and He is powerful. Hallelujah. And so it pays us to let the Holy Spirit come, the presence of God come, and teach us His ways so that we also have that presence of God motivating us to walk in His paths. These four things are necessary. And we don’t have a church service without any of them. But the most important part of these four things of prayer, praise and worship and thanksgiving and blessing and teaching the word—the most important part is His presence. The Bible says without Him we can do nothing, and the American church on the most part is trying to do this thing without Him.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Many people shall come and say, “Come, and let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, To the house of the God of Jacob; He will teach us His ways, And we shall walk in His paths.” For out of Zion shall go forth the law, And the word of the LORD from Jerusalem. He shall judge between the nations, And rebuke many people; They shall beat their swords into plowshares, And their spears into pruning hooks; Nation shall not lift up sword against nation, Neither shall they learn war anymore.
But you have come to Mount Zion and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, to an innumerable company of angels,

faqs.question: Why “magnifical” house?
faqs.answer: From 1 Chronicles 22:5 he says the house for the Lord must be exceeding magnifical—top quality fame and glory.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Now David said, “Solomon my son is young and inexperienced, and the house to be built for the LORD must be exceedingly magnificent, famous and glorious throughout all countries. I will now make preparation for it.” So David made abundant preparations before his death.

faqs.question: Can the gates of hell prevail against a united church?
faqs.answer: He says when fibers unite with word and Jesus as a three-fold cord, they become a group the gates of hell cannot prevail against.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And I also say to you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build My church, and the gates of Hades shall not prevail against it.

faqs.question: What is the church the pillar of?
faqs.answer: He says the church is the pillar and support of the truth—not opinions.

scriptures.text_nkjv: but if I am delayed, I write so that you may know how you ought to conduct yourself in the house of God, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth.

faqs.question: If you feel like a “half-breed,” can you serve?
faqs.answer: Yes. He says the Tyrian craftsman’s son worked with Israel’s skillful men, so you’re a candidate to be involved.

faqs.question: How large were David’s choir and orchestra?
faqs.answer: He says a choir of 288 and an orchestra of 4,000 prophesying with instruments by the Spirit.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Moreover David and the captains of the army separated for the service some of the sons of Asaph, of Heman, and of Jeduthun, who should prophesy with harps, stringed instruments, and cymbals. And the number of the skilled men performing their service was:

faqs.question: Who does he call the world’s chiefest sinner?
faqs.answer: Paul—who killed, blasphemed and persecuted—yet God saved him to help build the church.

faqs.question: What two things did God promise at the mercy seat?
faqs.answer: Meet with you (encounter) and speak with you from above the mercy seat.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And there I will meet with you, and I will speak with you from above the mercy seat, from between the two cherubim which are on the ark of the Testimony, about everything which I will give you in commandment to the children of Israel.

faqs.question: What happened when Paul reasoned with Felix?
faqs.answer: Felix trembled under righteousness, self-control and judgment to come, but would not commit to Christ.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Now as he reasoned about righteousness, self-control, and the judgment to come, Felix was afraid and answered, “Go away for now; when I have a convenient time I will call for you.”

faqs.question: What changes us into Christ’s image?
faqs.answer: Not inspirational preaching alone or a 12-step program—by the Spirit of the Lord, from glory to glory.

scriptures.text_nkjv: But we all, with unveiled face, beholding as in a mirror the glory of the Lord, are being transformed into the same image from glory to glory, just as by the Spirit of the Lord.

faqs.question: What is the most important part of a church service?
faqs.answer: His presence. Without Him we can do nothing, and he says much of the American church tries to do it without Him.
